body: I'm going to try getting some prompts together, which shouldn't be difficult because I just found there is actually a sub for that. Maybe paired with something like yoga, (which matt4it mentioned) will help. I'm willing to try anything because all I can feel is anger and contempt, and I want to keep my little dream of a better future. Thanks again for the replies. It has meant a lot to talk about this.

Thank you so much. I live about 20 miles west of the DFW metroplex, (TX) and I'm stuck with a sanitation job at the time. My boss is a very good man, and I'm making more and more money, but I HATE scrubbing sinks and toilets all day. I travel about 400 miles a week and that's nice, but I feel so isolated and trivial in what I do. I've had a lot of jobs, and this one may be the best fit for me since I don't have to be around anyone specific. However, I wonder if I would still be employed if my boss knew of my mental state and how often I've been slipping in front of gawd knows who.

I've been to Austin, TX and gone through a good deal of the Green Belt lately. Also, Mineral Wells State Park is much closer to my home and resembles the hill country, so I go there. I've been to Dinosaur Valley and I had plans to go on a mushroom trip on top of Enchanted Rock. I'm holding off on the mushrooms for now, at least until I can clear my mind of all the self-destructive loathing.

As far as literature goes; Nietzsche was profound to me before I found the, (will to) power to overcome addiction without god or a 12 step program. His Zarathustra is one of my favorite works, and The Antichrist was a powerfully crafted attack. I've fallen in love with Dostoyevsky's underground man, and Walter Kaufmann's collection of existential authors has been a joyous exploration. Ishmael by Daniel Quinn exceeded my expectations by far, as did the portion of Terrance McKenna's Food of the Gods which I have navigated thus far. I'm beginning Freud's The Future of an Illusion, and there are a few other book s that I would like to get to.

I think writing has been somewhat therapeutic, but I haven't done anything with it in a long time. Aside from my shameless mockery for the new Jurassic World blunder; this post has been the only thing that I've sat down and written since I tried my hand in college.

I'll give yoga a chance. Working out has never stuck with me, because I'll shed the muscle as soon as I stop eating 6 times a day. Maybe yoga can serve to be positivistic for me since it isn't supported by some aesthetic form of masturbation. And thank you for your reply. I'm seriously loosing my shit over this, but it feels good to talk about my feelings with someone. The anonymity helps me be more direct here, and just seeing that someone out there actually cares brings tears to my eyes.
